description.short: Historic imperial tribute tea dating to the Han dynasty — a revived yellow tea with gentle sweetness
description.overview: One of the earliest recorded teas in Chinese history, whose production completely ceased in the early 20th century before being painstakingly reconstructed in modern times from archival records.
description.aroma: Gentle, sweet, with mild nutty accents
description.taste: Sweet, smooth, completely free of sharp grassiness
description.processing: Plucking buds → pan-firing fixation → smothering in moist enclosures (men huang) → re-firing → final drying

history.origin: Recorded in historical texts dating back to the Han dynasty (over 2,000 years ago), making it one of China's earliest documented teas.
history.development: Supplied as imperial tribute for centuries; during the 20th century, production was nearly lost due to wars and social upheavals.
history.modern: The authentic yellow tea technique was revived in the early 1970s based on ancient agricultural treatises and surviving elders' memories, successfully restoring commercial production.
interestingFacts: It is among the few teas whose lineage spans over 2,000 years of documented Chinese tea history (despite an interruption prior to its mid-century revival).
Huoshan County is situated on the eastern slopes of the same Dabie Mountains where green Lu'an Gua Pian is grown, yet employs a fundamentally distinct processing philosophy.
